title: Build a Kenya intercity bus ticketing platform
before_you_start: A personal Supabase account ready so you can create a project (hosted and/or local CLI).
No starter app is provided on the desktop; you will build the Vue frontend and schema from scratch.

role.title: Full-stack engineer (Vue + Supabase)
role.company_context: Early product team building a digital ticketing product for Kenya intercity buses. Engineers own the passenger booking experience end to end: Postgres schema and Row Level Security on Supabase, plus a thin Vue client that talks to it. Hiring someone who can ship a credible MVP without a separate custom API layer unless they choose one.
day_to_day: Model routes, trips, seats/capacity, and bookings in Postgres on Supabase
Configure Auth and RLS so passengers only see and mutate their own bookings
Build Vue screens for search, trip selection, and booking confirmation
Seed enough Kenya corridor data to demo a real search → book path
Leave clear run notes so a teammate can reproduce the demo locally or against a hosted project
required_skills: Comfortable building a Vue SPA that calls a backend over HTTP
Can design a relational schema for trips and bookings and apply Supabase Auth + RLS
Can prevent obvious double-booking (constraints, transactions, or explicit holds)
Can document how to run the frontend and connect it to Supabase without leaking secrets
nice_to_have_skills: Supabase Edge Functions or RPC for atomic booking
Seat-map UI beyond a simple remaining-capacity counter
Local Supabase CLI workflow (supabase start / migrations)
constraints: Assessment is a greenfield MVP — no starter app, schema, or seed data is provided on the desktop
Primary UI must be Vue; primary backend must be Supabase (Postgres + Auth + RLS)
Do not require a real payment gateway; booking may create a confirmed or held ticket record only
Do not turn the challenge into operator fleet ops, live GPS tracking, or a multi-tenant marketplace

problem_statement.title: Ship a passenger booking MVP for Safari Coach ticketing
problem_statement.summary: You are building Safari Coach, a small digital ticketing product for intercity buses in Kenya. There are no starter files on the desktop — design and implement everything yourself. Use Supabase for the backend (Postgres, Auth, RLS) and Vue for the frontend that points at it. Seed enough realistic Kenya routes/trips (prices in KES) that a reviewer can search the Nairobi–Mombasa corridor (example fare around 2500 KES) and at least one secondary corridor such as Nairobi–Kisumu, pick a trip, and complete a booking as a signed-in passenger. Payments are out of scope: a successful booking should persist a confirmed or held ticket without a real payment provider.
outcomes: Stand up a Supabase project with Auth and a schema covering routes (or equivalent), trips, seat/capacity inventory, and bookings.
Apply RLS so booking and user-owned data are protected appropriately (anonymous users must not freely write or read other people’s bookings).
Build a Vue app that searches available trips (including Nairobi–Mombasa), selects a seat or ticket allocation, and completes a booking against that Supabase backend.
Leave short run notes so a reviewer can reproduce the demo (local Supabase CLI and/or hosted project setup without guessing).
constraints: Geography and currency: Kenya corridors and KES pricing (skeleton primary corridor Nairobi–Mombasa).
UI stack: Vue. Backend stack: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + RLS). A separate custom API is optional, not required.
No real payment gateway, PSP SDK, or card capture — booking creates a confirmed or held record only.
Do not commit service-role keys, passwords, or other secrets into the deliverable; document how env vars are set instead.
Scope is passenger booking MVP only — not operator dispatch, live vehicle tracking, or a multi-operator marketplace.
problem_statement.deliverables: A working Vue frontend, Supabase schema/migrations (or equivalent SQL the reviewer can apply), and a README with how to run both sides (local `supabase start` and/or hosted project URL plus anon-key setup). A reviewer should be able to create a user, search trips, book, and see the booking persisted.

rubric.name: Working end-to-end booking demo
rubric.summary: Shows a working Vue + Supabase flow from sign-in through a persisted booking.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Can a reviewer run (or follow documented hosted setup for) the Vue app against Supabase, sign in or sign up, search trips, and complete a booking that appears as a persisted row? Answer YES only if video or narrative shows a real Supabase write path end-to-end. Mock-only UI with no persisted booking, crash-on-start, or inferred “probably works” = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Schema and booking integrity
rubric.summary: Models trips and bookings coherently and prevents double-booking or overselling capacity.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the schema model trips and bookings coherently (routes/trips/capacity or seats), and is double-booking of the same seat or overselling capacity mitigated (unique constraint, transactional RPC, hold, or equivalent)? Answer YES only if both a coherent model and an oversell/double-book mitigation are visible. Unchecked concurrent inserts with no integrity control = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Auth and RLS quality
rubric.summary: Uses Auth on the booking path and RLS that stops anonymous writes and cross-user access.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is Auth used for the booking path, and does RLS (or equivalent server-side enforcement) prevent anonymous unrestricted writes and prevent one user from freely reading or mutating another user’s bookings? Answer YES only if both Auth on the booking path and non-trivial RLS/enforcement are present. Policies that are effectively `true` for booking writes, or no Auth on booking = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Vue UX clarity for search to book
rubric.summary: Makes search, trip selection, and booking confirmation understandable without reverse-engineering the UI.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is search → trip selection → book confirmation understandable without guessing, with empty and error states usable enough for a demo? Answer YES if a reviewer can follow the flow without reverse-engineering the UI. Broken or opaque flow that forces guessing next steps = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Reproducibility
rubric.summary: Documents how to run the app and does not commit secrets.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Do README (or equivalent notes) explain how to run frontend and backend, with no service-role or other secrets committed, such that a reviewer can reproduce without reverse-engineering undocumented steps? Answer YES only if run notes are sufficient and secrets are not committed. Empty/undocumented deliverable or committed service-role secrets = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

invariants: Keep the same skills_assessed and rubric structure/weights
Keep the same deliverable kinds and difficulty band (greenfield Vue + Supabase passenger booking MVP)
Do not replace Vue as the primary UI or Supabase as the primary backend
Do not add starter scaffolds, seed solutions, or answer keys under workspace/
Keep Kenya geography and KES pricing; no real payment gateway
Keep isomorphic difficulty: search → auth → book → persisted booking with RLS and oversell mitigation
